title: EPIC: P4 verifier matrix - Creusot, Verus and Kani per port and combined in one workspace
description:
Read WORKER-CONTRACT.md (workspace root) before starting. Human checkpoints (approve, record-ruling, accept-promotion, authorize-write grants) are run by the operator. Ligature is open-ended: file an epic #1 report only when Ligature fails at what it claims to do; record by-design limits as findings.

Agreed 2026-10-20 after P3 Stage 8C (#49). Plan the verifier matrix and reach consensus on it (P4-1 to P4-7) before any multi-verifier implementation starts.

What Ligature 1.4.2 already models (from its bundled schemas, not its source):
- verifier_policy.clusters (per-cluster owner) and verifier_policy.supporting (verifiers whose evidence backs the primary one);
- crates[] (several crates per workspace);
- verifier_backends for creusot, verus and kani (bridge checks);
- record-assurance intake for all three (--proof, --verus-json, --kani-crate; Verus residuals #125-#127).
- Gap seen so far: configure-crate has only a cargo-verus profile.
Upstream tickets are filed only for gaps the P4-5 probes confirm.

Limits independent of Ligature:
- single_verifier_system: a cluster whose closure spans two verifiers is CG1 ("cross-verifier composition has no soundness theorem") and can only be released degraded at the harness-tested ceiling. Three verifiers can share a workspace in separate clusters, but any cross-verifier dependency comes out degraded by design.
- Creusot (nightly-2026-04-21, creusot_std) and Verus (1.95.0, vstd, verus!) need separate crates. Kani harnesses (#[cfg(kani)]) overlay either.

Axis A, which verifier proves which port:

| Port | Creusot | Verus | Kani |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 date (integer arithmetic) | done | P4-9 | P4-10 |
| P2 SwissTable (generics, ghost maps, unsafe, SIMD) | P4-11 | P4-8 (complete the closure) | P4-12 |
| P3 crypto (bit arithmetic, byte buffers) | P4-13 | P4-14 | done |

Axis B, combining verifiers:
- supporting verifiers (P4-15);
- verifiers mixed inside one closure (P4-16, supersedes #50);
- a cluster split with a boundary contract (P4-17, supersedes #51);
- all six directed cross-cluster pairs (P4-18);
- all three verifiers in one workspace (P4-19).
Already done: Kani inside a deductive Creusot closure (#23).

Open question for P4-7: whether a fourth C++ project, or a synthetic probe, is needed for CG6 (dependency cycles between clusters) and G15 (non-pairwise protocols), which no current port exercises. Results feed #69 through P4-20.

comments.content: Correction from P4-3 (#157): the Axis A row 'P2 SwissTable (generics, ghost maps, unsafe, SIMD)' describes Abseil, not the port. The port is monomorphic u64 with initialized Vec storage and scalar 16-byte groups (scope cuts swisstable-verus-008/-001/-002); only the spec-level Map/Seq/Set model is real. VERIFIER-MATRIX.md rows A4-A6 are corrected (root 9b66a39). Kani can verify upstream's SSE2 group masks if a cell adds that implementation; raw MaybeUninit slots cannot be checked for initialization by Kani 0.67 (swisstable-kani-001).

title: [p4 matrix] P4-7 Consensus checkpoint: approve the matrix, the workspace layout and the fourth-project decision

comments.content: Decision items for the consensus checkpoint, from P4-2/P4-3: (1) P1 on Kani (#164): YearMonthDay.C002 is stated over an Int logic function Kani cannot express; choose between comparing from_days with an i64 reference implementation and carrying C002 through C007 plus range checks (date-creusot/analysis/p4-verifier-fit/). (2) P2 on Kani (#166): verify only the current scalar port, or also add a real SSE2 GroupProbe (Kani proves upstream's SSE2 masks equal to scalar) and/or a raw MaybeUninit slot variant (Kani cannot check its initialization, swisstable-kani-001; needs a shadow init map). (3) Whether Kani evidence for P2's Verus scope cuts (-004 probe coverage, -033 slot change) is wanted as supporting evidence in the B1 rows.

More decision items from P4-4 (#158): (4) P3 deductive cells (#167, #168): for std calls without verifier specs (rotate_left, from_le_bytes, to_le_bytes, fill in both; copy_from_slice and slice try_into in Verus; extend_from_slice in Creusot), use trusted specs (assume_specification / extern_spec!, unchecked) or rewrite production code into shifts, masks and loops under the 2580-case oracle. (5) Poly1305 scope for those cells: attempt functional correctness (h = (h + m)*r mod 2^130-5 over 26-bit limbs; deep) or declare the Poly1305 part partial and keep its functional evidence with Kani and the oracle.

Review reminder: this operator checkpoint must cover its FULL issue spec, beyond the #160 layout handoff. Alongside the matrix/verifier assignments, crate ownership/source sharing, exact toolchain pins, write-set/creation routes, output roots, and closure policy, decide (1) a fourth C++ project versus synthetic probes for CG6/G15, and (2) the exact scope of P4-8 through P4-19. These remain pending operator decisions; this comment approves no option and changes no implementation authorization.

Bit arithmetic needs #[bitwise_proof] on each mask/shift function with specs compared on u64; u64 division is not available in logic, and hash>>7 == hash/128 needs a lemma (swisstable-creusot-001). The cell is a full Pearlite rewrite: 66 requires, 71 ensures, 63 loop invariants, 44 spec fns, 7 proof fns. Probes: swisstable-verus/analysis/p4-verifier-fit/probes/creusot/.

subissues.title: [deliverables] Backfill <pilot>/PORT-GAPS.md for date-creusot (P1) from its findings and README
subissues.description: Read WORKER-CONTRACT.md §6.5 first. P1 (date-creusot) finished before PORT-GAPS.md existed. Go through date-creusot/findings/limitations.jsonl, README.md and analysis/ and write date-creusot/PORT-GAPS.md covering every C++->Rust transfer gap found in P1. Examples: Creusot logic-emission limits that forced inlined contracts (cross-module logic twins, bool logic fns opaque), the round_trip missing-ensures diagnosis, const fn reach, era-arithmetic overflow obligations, codesight's C++-header misclassification, subset scope cuts relative to HowardHinnant/date, and oracle coverage limits. Each entry uses the §6.5 fields, links its finding ids, and has a generalizable lesson. Documentation only: touch only date-creusot/PORT-GAPS.md. No ligature pipeline commands that write. Post ONE evidence comment listing the entries. Don't close this issue.
